This script prepares CR-birding data for upload to a [GBIF IPT](https://gbif.org/ipt).

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

Install crbirding package:

```{r}
# devtools::install_github("inbo/crbirding")
```

Load libraries:

```{r}
library(here)
library(crbirding)
library(readr)
```

## Set user-defined values

```{r}
project_id <- "LARGE_GULLS"
dataset_id <- NULL # Republish with GBIF DOI
dataset_name <- "CR-Birding - Large gulls, blue ring with 4 letters (third=A E or O)"
license <- "CC0-1.0"
rights_holder <- "INBO"
```

## Create and write Darwin Core

Read data and set directory:

```{r}
data <- readr::read_csv(here::here("data", "raw", project_id, "crbirding_export.csv"))
dir <- here::here("data", "processed", project_id, "dwc")
```

Data transformation:

```{r}
dwc <- crbirding::write_dwc(
  data = data,
  directory = dir,
  dataset_id = dataset_id,
  dataset_name = dataset_name,
  license = license,
  rights_holder = rights_holder
)
```

## Post-processing for INBO-datasets

The colour-ring data was previously managed in a different database. The old data is less precise. An analysis of the full data export shows that all entries from October 1st, 2020, onwards have exact coordinates in decimal degrees. Older data had lower precision (like 53°12'N - 03°10'E) and were later transformed. Consequently, October 1st, 2020, is the cutoff date to reset the coordinate precision. Therefore, coordinates and coordinateUncertaintyInMeters before this date are set to a lower precision.

```{r, eval = TRUE}
migration_date <- "2020-10-01"
dwc$occurrence <-
  dwc$occurrence |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    decimalLatitude = dplyr::if_else(eventDate < migration_date, round(decimalLatitude, 2), decimalLatitude),
    decimalLongitude = dplyr::if_else(eventDate < migration_date, round(decimalLongitude, 2), decimalLongitude),
    coordinateUncertaintyInMeters = dplyr::if_else(eventDate < migration_date, 1500, coordinateUncertaintyInMeters)
  )

readr::write_csv(occurrence, file.path(dir, "occurrence.csv"), na = "")
```
